explanation: For every possible left-subtree size, recursively generate all left and right shapes and combine every pair under a new root. Zero nodes contributes one null tree. The method returns roots; the wrapper serializes each root into full breadth-first 1/0 shape markers. Subtree roots may be shared between different output trees; this exercise judges shape rather than disjoint ownership.
timeComplexity: O(n·Cₙ) safe upper bound, including enumeration and wrapper serialization of Cₙ shapes with n nodes each; subproblems are recomputed rather than memoized. There are Cₙ ordered shapes and each observed encoding has 2n+1 markers.
spaceComplexity: O(n·Cₙ) upper bound including all returned trees and temporary subtree families; recursion depth is O(n). Returned shapes/encodings dominate storage; recursion depth is bounded by n.

correctness: Every nonempty ordered binary tree has one left-subtree size and one ordered pair of subtree shapes. Trying every size and pair generates it exactly once by induction; the null tree is the base case. Wrapper serialization preserves null-child positions, distinguishing left-only from right-only trees.
walkthrough: With two nodes, left size 0 combines null with a leaf, and left size 1 combines a leaf with null. Return these two roots. The wrapper observes [1,0,1,0,0] and [1,1,0,0,0], respectively; these marker arrays are not the method return type.
edgeCases: Zero nodes returns a list containing a null root; the wrapper encodes it as [0].
Left and right subtrees are ordered: mirror-image shapes are different.
Do not return marker arrays from the native tree-returning callable.
